title: Substructure Analyzer: A User-Friendly Workflow for Rapid Exploration and Accurate Analysis of Cellular Bodies in Fluorescence Microscopy Images
protocol: Use the Merge Channels block exclusively.
Remove all other blocks from the protocol.
Save the protocol as Merge Channels.
Access the boxes to set parameters for each channel.
Enter the channel number X in box 1, 5, or 9 (for example: 0=Red).
Specify the folder containing images of channel X in box 2, 6, or 10.
Enter the separator used for image names in box 3, 7, or 11.
Choose a colormap model number to use for visualization in Icy in box 4, 8, or 12.
Use display boxes (boxes 23, 24, or 25) to visualize the sequence of each channel directly.
Write the smallest channel value on the upper line and the highest one on the bottom line.
Enter the format extension for merged images in box 28 (.tif, .gif, .jpg, .bmp, or .png).
Set the Intensity classes parameter in box HK-Means.
Define approximate minimum and maximum sizes of objects to be detected in pixels in box HK-Means.
Evaluate object size by drawing a ROI around the object of interest manually.
Access size of the ROI (Interior in pixels) on the image or through the ROI statistics window.
Optimize detection of object borders in box Active Contours.
Run the workflow for marker-based watershed segmentation.
Open dialog boxes for HK-means parameters and Marker-based Watershed algorithm.
Click YES to apply the same parameters for all images (fully-automated version).
Manually apply the HK-Means plugin on the image when prompted.
Select Export ROIs option in the HK-Means plugin box.
Apply best parameters to have ROIs containing a maximum of foreground pixels and optimize individualization of foreground objects.
Close the image directly after finding optimal ROIs.
Remove unwanted ROIs and close image after the first segmentation method completes.
Select OK to remove ROIs of mis-segmented objects from the opened image.
Delete individual ROIs by placing cursor on their border and using the “Delete” button.
Close the image after deleting all unwanted ROIs.
Repeat the procedure after completion of the second segmentation step.
Determine and adjust internal markers if NO was selected for full-automatization.
Click OK in the information box asking to determine and adjust internal markers.
Go to Plugins | MorphoLibJ | Minima and Maxima|Extended Min & Max within ImageJ interface.
Select Extended Minima in Operation.
Preview the result of the transformation on the automatically opened image.
Move the dynamic until optimal markers are observed, leading to one marker per object.
If necessary, apply additional morphological operations like “Opening” or “Closing” using MorphoLibJ.
Keep the final image of markers open and close all other images ending with the input image for Extended Minima operation.
Click No if an ImageJ box asks to save changes on this image.
Determine how many images with Information Boxes should appear in the Nb of images with Information Box (box 14).
Set the channel of the cytoplasmic signal in Channel cytoplasm (box 1).
Write the format used to save images of segmented nuclei in Extension segmented nuclei (box 2).
Write the name of the folder containing segmented nuclei in Text (box 3).
Set the format for saving segmented objects images in Format of images of segmented cytoplasms (box 4).
Create a folder to save images of segmented cytoplasms.
Name the folder (e.g., Segmented cytoplasms).
Set parameters for boxes Gaussian filter and Active Contours.
Run the workflow as detailed in part 7.
Select the adapted block for fluorescence analysis.
Perform detection and analysis of coilin foci in one channel within the nucleus.
Perform detection and analysis of coilin and 53BP1 foci in two channels within the nucleus.
Perform detection and analysis of Coilin foci in one or two channels, specifically inside the nuclei and their corresponding cytoplasm.
Calculate the percentage of signal from one channel in two cellular compartments for global translocation analysis.
Export calculated percentages of nuclear and cytoplasmic signals for each image in the final “Results” spreadsheet.
Optimize the Fluorescence Analysis E block for nucleus/cytoplasm translocation assay at the single-cell level.
Ensure efficient segmentation of nucleus and cytoplasm.
Link the output0 (File) of the Select Folder block to the folder input of the chosen fluorescence analysis block.
Set parameters for Fluorescence Analysis A: 1 Channel, B: 2 Channels in the same compartment, and C: 2 Channels in two compartments.
Write the name of the folder containing images of segmented objects preceded by a backslash in the Folder images ROI box.
Set spot detection parameters in Wavelet Spot Detector Block for each channel.
Define scale(s) (spot size).
Adjust sensitivity of detection (default value is 100, minimum value is 0).
Optionally, set an interval of size to filter segmented objects by spot size in Filter ROI by size box.
Filter nuclei by size in the box 2 Channels in two compartments if required.
Filter cytoplasm by size in the box 2 Channels in two compartments if required.
Optional: In the box Filter spots by size, filter detected spots according to their size (in pixels) to remove unwanted artifacts.
Manually estimate spot size using Detection and Tracking | Spot Detector plugin.
Select Export to ROI in Output options.
Apply an additional filter on detected spots as needed.
Set a threshold for the area in pixels of analyzed spots if required.
Write the name of the folder containing images of segmented objects in Folder images boxes.
Identify the two types of ROI as ROI a and ROI b for Global Translocation analysis.
Write the name of the folder containing segmented nuclei in Folder images segmented nuclei box.
Write the name of the folder containing segmented cytoplasms in Folder images segmented cytoplasms box.
Enter the channel of the signal in Channel signal box.
Remove the connection between the selected block and the block Select Folder.
Place the wanted block at the 1st rank.
Click on the link directly to the right of folder in the upper left corner of the wanted block.
In the Open dialog box, double-click on the folder containing the merged images.
Then, click on Open.
Click on Run to start the workflow.
If necessary, stop the processing by clicking on the Stop button.
Before running the workflow, remove unused blocks and save the new protocol with another name.
When the open dialog box appears, double-click on the folder containing the merged images.
Then, click on Open.
The workflow automatically runs.
